translations.text: We read that the Savior went along weary from travel. At midday, know this, he sat down by a well.
A woman came quickly from Samaria to draw water; he was still sitting there.
He asked the woman who had come there to give him a drink. His disciples were off getting his food.
"Why do you ask, good man, that I give you a drink? Christ knows, the Jews indeed make no use of our food."
"Woman, if you knew what God's gift is, and recognized the one you were talking with, you would ask him to grant you his living spring."
"This well that I came running to from home is so deep, and you have no vessel to draw it with. Where can you, good man, get a living spring?
"Surely you are not greater among people than Jacob? He gave us this well; he drank from it, and so did his men; his small livestock used the water."
"Whoever drinks this water will thirst for it again; but whoever drinks mine, thirst will leave him alone. It springs up in his breast forever, with delight."
"Lord, I beg you, give me the water, so that I no longer have to run here thirsty every day."
"Woman, turn back [?], fetch your husband here." She said that she lived so, that she had no husband.
"I know that you speak the truth, that you have no husband. Before this you had five to support you.
"Of this you may be sure: the one you have now is not yours." "Lord, it seems to me from you that you may be a prophet.
"Those born before us prayed here on the mountain. Our ancestors sought mercy here; yet you say that the chosen place of prayer is in Jerusalem."
